name: Maple Syrup Urine Disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ACMG ACT Sheet and biochemical criteria for MSUD

criteria.description: Elevated plasma branched-chain amino acids (leucine, isoleucine, valine) on newborn screening or plasma amino acid analysis
Elevated urinary branched-chain alpha-ketoacids (alpha-ketoisocaproic acid, alpha-keto-beta-methylvaleric acid, alpha-ketoisovaleric acid)
Reduced BCKD enzyme activity in fibroblasts or leukocytes
Biallelic pathogenic variants in BCKDHA, BCKDHB, or DBT genes
Maple syrup or burnt sugar odor of urine, earwax, or sweat

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Elevated branched-chain amino acids with presence of alloisoleucine in plasma, confirmed by enzyme assay or genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Classic MSUD presents in the first week of life with encephalopathy. Intermediate, intermittent, and thiamine-responsive forms have later onset and milder presentation. Early detection via newborn screening is critical.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated plasma branched chain amino acids

laboratory: Markedly elevated plasma leucine (often >2000 micromol/L in classic form)
Metabolic acidosis with elevated anion gap
imaging: MRI brain: diffusion restriction in myelinated areas during acute crisis (globus pallidus, cerebral peduncles, posterior limb of internal capsule)
MRI showing white matter edema (diffuse cerebral edema) in severe crises
CT may show cerebral edema in acute presentation
genetic: BCKDHA gene mutations (E1alpha subunit; type IA)
BCKDHB gene mutations (E1beta subunit; type IB, most common)
DBT gene mutations (E2 subunit; type II)
DLD gene mutations (E3 subunit; shared with pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase)
Homozygous BCKDHA c.1312T>A (Y438N) founder mutation in Mennonite population
other: Newborn screening by tandem mass spectrometry (leucine/isoleucine elevation)
BCKD enzyme activity assay in cultured fibroblasts or leukocytes
Bedside urine DNPH test for screening
Thiamine responsiveness testing in intermediate or mild forms

distinguishingFeatures: Organic acidemias have different amino acid and organic acid profiles
Propionic and methylmalonic acidemia have elevated propionylcarnitine
Sepsis has positive blood cultures and elevated inflammatory markers
Normal amino acid profile in sepsis
MSUD may mimic sepsis in neonatal period
Urea cycle defects have hyperammonemia as primary finding
Normal branched-chain amino acids in urea cycle defects
Respiratory alkalosis rather than metabolic acidosis
PKU has elevated phenylalanine, not branched-chain amino acids
PKU does not cause acute neonatal encephalopathy
Different amino acid pattern on screening

redFlags: Neonatal encephalopathy with maple syrup odor (emergency: begin leucine-free formula immediately)
Plasma leucine >1500 micromol/L (high risk for cerebral edema and permanent brain injury)
Metabolic decompensation during intercurrent illness or fasting in known MSUD patients
references: Strauss KA, et al. Maple Syrup Urine Disease. In: Adam MP, et al., eds. GeneReviews. University of Washington, Seattle; 2006 [Updated 2020].
Frazier DM, et al. Nutrition management guideline for maple syrup urine disease. Mol Genet Metab. 2014;112(3):210-7.
Blackburn PR, et al. Maple syrup urine disease: mechanisms and management. Appl Clin Genet. 2017;10:57-66.
Morton DH, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of maple syrup disease: a study of 36 patients. Pediatrics. 2002;109(6):999-1008.
